title: Subscriptions, Resource Groups, and Resources
description: Learn how to work with subscriptions, create and manage resource groups, organize resources, and use tags and locks.

data.text: Now that you understand the hierarchy, it is time to work with the three levels you will use every day: subscriptions, resource groups, and resources. You will also learn how tags and locks help you keep things organized and protected.

A subscription is your billing boundary and access boundary. Each subscription has limits on how many resources of each type you can create. You can have multiple subscriptions for different environments, such as development and production.

A resource group is a logical container for resources that share the same lifecycle. For example, you might put a web app, its database, and its storage account in the same resource group so you can deploy and delete them together.

data.title: Create a Resource Group with Azure CLI
data.code:
# Create a resource group in the East US region
az group create \
  --name MyAppResourceGroup \
  --location eastus

# List resource groups in your subscription
az group list --output table

# Tag a resource group
az group update \
  --name MyAppResourceGroup \
  --tags environment=production team=backend

data.text: Resources are the actual Azure services you create, such as a virtual machine, a storage account, or a web app. When you create a resource, you must specify which resource group it belongs to. The resource's name must be unique across all of Azure for its type.

Tags are key-value pairs you attach to resources or resource groups. They help you organize, track costs, and find resources. For example, you might tag all production resources with `environment=production` and all frontend resources with `team=frontend`.

data.title: Common Tag Uses
items: Track costs by department or project
Identify the owner of a resource
Group resources by environment (dev, staging, prod)
Automate deployments based on tag values

data.text: A lock prevents a resource from being accidentally deleted or modified. You can apply a **CanNotDelete** lock, which allows reading and modifying the resource but blocks deletion, or a **ReadOnly** lock, which blocks all changes.

terms.definition: A billing and access boundary for Azure resources.
A container that holds related Azure resources sharing the same lifecycle.
A key-value pair attached to a resource or resource group for organization and cost tracking.
A setting that prevents a resource from being accidentally deleted or modified.

data.title: Try It Yourself
data.description: Use the Azure CLI to create a resource group, tag it, and create a resource inside it.
steps: Run `az login` to sign in to your Azure account
Create a resource group named `learn-rg` in the `westus` region
Add a tag `project=learning` to the resource group
Create a storage account named `learnstorage12345` inside the resource group
data.expectedOutcome: You should see the new resource group in the Azure Portal with your tag applied, and the storage account listed inside it.
